lineage.strategy: Use fresh SEC contract-quality and cash-deployment evidence to separate real demand visibility from backlog firmness and funding risk.

observedWeaknesses.observation: Quanta reported $53.44B total backlog and $33.55B RPO, but backlog includes estimated MSA orders/renewals and non-fixed-price contracts; many customer contracts can be terminated on short notice.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Headline backlog is not uniformly equivalent to firm contracted revenue, so conversion quality matters alongside backlog growth.

observedWeaknesses.observation: Six-month acquisition cash use was about $930.3M and capex $451.0M while commercial paper outstanding was $448M, despite strong $1.49B operating cash flow and substantial available liquidity.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Execution remains capital intensive; resilience depends on continued cash conversion while acquisitions and capex stay elevated.

risks.risk: Backlog quality may be weaker than the headline total implies because MSA estimates and terminable contracts can fail to convert at assumed volumes or timing.
Sustained acquisition/capex intensity could pressure funding flexibility if operating cash conversion deteriorates.

falsifiers.condition: RPO and realized revenue conversion remain strong while operating cash flow continues to cover capital deployment without material leverage deterioration.
falsifiers.effect: Would reduce both backlog-quality and funding-resilience concerns.

improvementPaths: Track RPO-to-revenue conversion separately from broader backlog and monitor cash conversion against acquisition/capex deployment.

unknowns.unknown: The cited filing does not establish what fraction of total backlog will convert on the timing implied by headline backlog growth.

recommendation: Use as source-addressed risk/falsifier evidence; Alpha retains numeric underwriting authority.
